name_ta: Ligamentum collaterale ulnare articulationis metacarpophalangealis pollicis
name_common: Ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint

attachments.landmark_a: head of 1st metacarpal (ulnar/radial condyle, dorsal to the midline axis of rotation)
attachments.landmark_b: base of proximal phalanx of thumb (ulnar/radial tubercle)

bands.name: Ulnar collateral ligament of thumb MCP joint

attachments.landmark_b: ulnar tubercle at base of proximal phalanx of thumb

bands.mechanical_role: the primary restraint to radial (valgus) angulation and rotational stress at the thumb MCP joint during pinch and grasp; its proper (MCP-spanning) fibers are taut in flexion while its accessory fibers (spanning the volar plate/sesamoid) are taut in extension
bands.function_note: The single most clinically important ligament of the hand after the flexor pulley system -- its acute rupture from forced radial deviation/hyperextension of the thumb ('gamekeeper's thumb', historically described in Scottish gamekeepers from twisting rabbits' necks, and the acute sporting equivalent 'skier's thumb' from a ski pole strap) is common and, if a complete distal-insertion tear retracts proximal to the interposed adductor pollicis aponeurosis (a 'Stener lesion'), the ligament cannot heal without surgical repair because the aponeurosis physically blocks its path back to the phalangeal insertion. Distinguishing a Stener lesion (surgical) from a non-displaced partial tear (splintable) is the central clinical decision this ligament drives.
bands.source: Chang AL, Merkow DB, Bookman JS, Glickel SZ (2023) 'Thumb Metacarpophalangeal Joint Ulnar Collateral Ligament Injuries: Management and Biomechanical Evaluation.' J Am Acad Orthop Surg 31(1):7-16, doi:10.5435/JAAOS-D-22-00112 -- retrieved via PubMed.

function: Stabilizes the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint against radial (valgus) stress, which is generated repeatedly and forcefully during normal pinch and key-grip; its clinical importance rests on the ligament's very common traumatic rupture and the 'Stener lesion' pattern that prevents non-operative healing of complete tears.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Chang AL, Merkow DB, Bookman JS, Glickel SZ (2023) 'Thumb Metacarpophalangeal Joint Ulnar Collateral Ligament Injuries: Management and Biomechanical Evaluation.' J Am Acad Orthop Surg 31(1):7-16, doi:10.5435/JAAOS-D-22-00112 -- retrieved via PubMed.

name_ta: Ligamentum collaterale radiale articulationis metacarpophalangealis pollicis
name_common: Radial collateral ligament of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint

attachments.landmark_b: radial tubercle at base of proximal phalanx of thumb

bands.name: Radial collateral ligament of thumb MCP joint

attachments.landmark_b: radial tubercle at base of proximal phalanx of thumb

bands.mechanical_role: restrains ulnar (varus) angulation and rotational stress at the thumb MCP joint; biomechanically weaker and injured far less often than the UCL, since forced ulnar deviation of the thumb is a much less common mechanism than forced radial deviation
bands.function_note: The UCL's companion structure on the opposite side of the joint. Radial collateral ligament injury is a real but markedly less common clinical entity than UCL ('gamekeeper's/skier's thumb') injury, typically from a hyperadduction/ulnar-directed force (e.g. a fall onto an abducted, radially-loaded thumb); a Stener-equivalent lesion is comparatively rare here because the abductor pollicis brevis tendon/adductor aponeurosis relationship that blocks UCL healing is not mirrored on the radial side.
bands.source: Daley D, Geary M, Gaston RG (2020) 'Thumb Metacarpophalangeal Ulnar and Radial Collateral Ligament Injuries.' Clin Sports Med 39(2):443-455, doi:10.1016/j.csm.2019.12.003 -- retrieved via PubMed.

function: Stabilizes the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint against ulnar (varus) stress -- the collateral ligament pair partner of the ulnar collateral ligament, completing the joint's medial-lateral restraint.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Daley D, Geary M, Gaston RG (2020) 'Thumb Metacarpophalangeal Ulnar and Radial Collateral Ligament Injuries.' Clin Sports Med 39(2):443-455, doi:10.1016/j.csm.2019.12.003 -- retrieved via PubMed.

name_ta: Ligamenta collateralia et plicae palmares digitorum manus
name_common: Finger MCP/PIP collateral ligament and volar plate complex

attachments.landmark_a: metacarpal heads (2nd-5th digits) / proximal phalanx heads (PIP level) -- dorsal aspect of each condyle
attachments.landmark_b: proximal/middle phalanx bases, palmar tubercles and volar plate

bands.name: Proper and accessory collateral ligaments (MCP and PIP joints, digits 2-5)

attachments.landmark_a: eccentric (dorsal-of-center) tubercle on each metacarpal/proximal-phalanx head
attachments.landmark_b: palmar aspect of the base of the next phalanx (proper ligament) and the volar plate (accessory ligament)

bands.mechanical_role: the eccentric, off-axis origin of each collateral ligament from the condylar head means the proper ligament is slack in extension and taut in flexion (cam mechanism), while the accessory ligament -- inserting on the volar plate rather than bone -- is reciprocally more taut in extension
bands.function_note: This same cam-shaped condylar geometry, repeated near-identically at every MCP and PIP joint of the four fingers, is exactly why a finger immobilized in extension for more than a short period stiffens into flexion contracture ('collateral ligament shortening') -- splinting a hand joint should be done with the MCP flexed and IP joints extended to keep every collateral ligament at its longest length ('safe' or intrinsic-plus position). Modeled here as one representative complex rather than 4 digits x 2 joints x 2 ligaments (8 near-identical structures), matching this atlas's convention (see the flexor tendon pulley system) of modeling the hand's repetitive systems as one entity with representative parts rather than exhaustively enumerating every digit.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Volar (palmar) plates (MCP and PIP joints, digits 2-5)

attachments.landmark_a: firmly fixed to the base of the more distal phalanx at each joint
attachments.landmark_b: loosely/membranously attached proximally, continuous with the flexor tendon sheath

bands.mechanical_role: a thick fibrocartilaginous floor to each MCP/PIP joint that checks hyperextension while permitting full flexion, and forms the fixed floor over which the flexor tendons glide
bands.function_note: The PIP joint's volar plate is the more clinically significant of the two levels: a hyperextension injury commonly avulses it from its distal (firm) attachment rather than tearing its substance, producing the classic PIP 'dorsal fracture-dislocation' / volar plate injury pattern seen in ball-sport 'jammed finger' presentations; because the proximal attachment is loose and membranous while the distal attachment is firm, the plate normally folds like a hinge during flexion without buckling into the joint.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

function: Represents the collateral ligament + volar plate arrangement present at every MCP and PIP joint of the four fingers: paired eccentric collateral ligaments providing side-to-side stability with a flexion-dependent cam mechanism, and a volar fibrocartilaginous plate resisting hyperextension -- together the dominant static stabilizers of finger joint alignment during grip and the structures most often injured in finger dislocations and 'jammed finger' sprains.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
